name: Cappadocia · Göreme
tagline: Fairy chimneys, cave churches and balloons at dawn
summary: Base yourself in Göreme and walk to the open-air museum and the valleys. Give one dawn to the balloons, one day to the valleys on foot and one to an underground city and the Ihlara gorge.
seasonNote: Winters are snowy and cold and balloons are often grounded by wind; July and August are hot and dry.
arrival: Fly to Kayseri (1 hour away) or Nevşehir (40 minutes) and book a shared shuttle to your hotel in advance; overnight buses run from Istanbul.
gettingAround: Göreme is walkable and the valleys start at its edge. Local buses link Göreme, Uçhisar, Avanos and Ürgüp; the far sights need a tour or rental car.
cashTip: Museums price tickets in euros but take cards in lira; carry lira for village buses, tea gardens and small cafes.
foodTip: Order testi kebabı, a stew sealed and baked in a clay pot, along with mantı dumplings and gözleme flatbread.
buyTip: Avanos is the pottery town; carpets and onyx are sold everywhere, so compare before buying.
baseArea: Göreme for walking access; Uçhisar for quiet and views

connections.note: To Kayseri or Nevşehir, plus an hour's shuttle.
Overnight bus; no direct flights most of the year.

items.name: Göreme Open Air Museum
items.summary: A cluster of rock-cut monastery churches with Byzantine frescoes from the 10th to 12th centuries.
items.expect: Tour groups fill the small churches from mid-morning; photos are not allowed inside.
items.tip: Arrive at opening and pay the extra fee for the Dark Church, which has the best-preserved frescoes.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult in local currency, not a live ticket quote; check current prices and what is included.
items.sourceNote: Editorial selection. Durations, spending allowances and itinerary advice are planning estimates; check opening days and prices with the venue before you go.
whyVisit: A cluster of rock-cut monastery churches with Byzantine frescoes from the 10th to 12th centuries.
It is the clearest look at why monks carved this landscape and it is a UNESCO World Heritage site.
visitFlow: Walk 20 minutes uphill from Göreme.
Circle the churches clockwise, ending at the Dark Church.
items.bestFor: Visitors interested in history and context and sacred places
tradeoffs: Tour groups fill the small churches from mid-morning; photos are not allowed inside.
Arrive at opening and pay the extra fee for the Dark Church, which has the best-preserved frescoes.

items.name: Sunrise hot air balloon flight
items.summary: An hour drifting over the valleys with a hundred other balloons at first light.
items.expect: A pickup around 5 am; flights are cancelled on windy days, most often in winter.
items.tip: Book for your first morning so you can rebook if the wind cancels it.
items.priceNote: Planning estimate per adult in local currency, not a live ticket quote; check current prices and what is included.

whyVisit: An hour drifting over the valleys with a hundred other balloons at first light.

items.name: Uçhisar Castle
items.summary: A hollowed rock citadel at the highest point of the region, with a view over every valley.
items.expect: A steep climb on uneven steps; busy at sunset.
items.tip: Walk down afterwards through Pigeon Valley back to Göreme, about an hour.

items.name: Derinkuyu Underground City
items.summary: A city dug eight levels down, with stables, chapels and ventilation shafts, that once sheltered thousands.
items.expect: Low, narrow tunnels; not for anyone uneasy in tight spaces.
items.tip: Go early or late to avoid queues in the one-way passages.

items.tip: One ticket covers both sites; start at Paşabağ before the buses arrive.

items.summary: Trails through pink and ochre rock past hidden chapels to a ridge that glows at sunset.
items.expect: Unmarked forks in the trail; download an offline map.
items.tip: Start from Çavuşin two hours before sunset and finish at the Red Valley viewpoint.

items.name: Ihlara Valley
items.summary: A green river gorge lined with painted rock churches, an hour and a half from Göreme.
items.expect: About 400 steps down; the full walk is 14 km, though most do a 4 km section.
items.tip: The 'Green Tour' combines the valley with Derinkuyu and Selime Monastery in one day.
